title: AI is an Amplifier: Scale High Performance, Not Dysfunction
gist: Nathen Harvey (Google Cloud DORA) presents the 2025 DORA findings from a survey of nearly 5,000 people: about 90% use AI at work and feel more productive, yet AI raises software delivery instability, so AI is an amplifier of the underlying organization. He lays out seven capabilities that turn adoption into outcomes, the J-curve instability and verification tax, seven team profiles, and a provocative call to rethink code reviews.

insights.claim: The 2025 DORA survey, run June 13 to July 21, 2025 with nearly 5,000 respondents plus qualitative interviews, found about 90% of respondents use AI professionally, so DORA will stop asking whether people use AI at work.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey
insights.so_what: AI use at work is effectively universal among software professionals, so adoption alone no longer differentiates.
insights.locator: Ninety percent of our survey respondents said yes

insights.claim: About 35% of respondents rely on AI little or not at all, a majority rely on it for their tasks, and the median respondent interacts with AI for about two hours a day, roughly the 10-30% of time engineers are said to spend writing code.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey
insights.so_what: Reliance, not mere use, is the better indicator of dependence and risk if tools fail.
insights.locator: What we see here is that about 35% of our respondents

insights.claim: Respondents feel more productive and engaged and see code quality improving, with about 5% reporting decreased productivity and about 10% saying code quality is a little worse.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey
insights.so_what: Perceived gains are broad but self-reported; objective metrics tell a more mixed story.
insights.locator: Your perceived impact on individual productivity, it's going up.

insights.claim: About 30% trust AI-generated output a little or not at all, and Harvey argues both extremes (trusting a great deal or not at all) are wrong and that the right stance is somewhat trusting.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey
insights.so_what: Calibrated trust is the target; verification practices must scale with AI use.
insights.quote: You should not trust it a great deal.
insights.locator: how much do you trust the quality that AI is generating?

themes.theme: AI as amplifier and the instability tax

insights.claim: DORA's central finding is that AI's primary role is as an amplifier: the greatest returns come from focusing on the underlying organizational system, and without that foundation AI creates localized pockets of productivity lost to downstream chaos.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey
insights.so_what: Invest in delivery system health, not just tool licences, to capture AI returns.
insights.quote: AI's primary role in software development is that of an amplifier.
insights.locator: If I summarize that entire 2025 report for you in three slides

insights.claim: In DORA's simulation, raising AI adoption alone increased individual effectiveness the most and also raised team and organizational performance, valuable work time, code quality, product performance and throughput, but software delivery instability rose, while burnout and friction stayed near zero.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey
insights.so_what: AI boosts output metrics but worsens change failure outcomes unless offset by practices.
insights.locator: Individual effectiveness increased the most.

insights.claim: Software delivery instability, measured by how often production pushes force rollbacks or hot fixes, rose with AI; in 2024 instability rose and throughput fell, whereas in 2025 throughput improved, consistent with a J-curve of adopting new technology.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey
insights.so_what: Expect a dip after initial gains; plan for the instability and verification tax.
insights.locator: like software delivery instability is getting worse

insights.claim: Harvey worries burnout and cognitive overload will worsen in the next research because developers managing several agents bounce between tasks, noting handing someone a new tool did not help burnout in the 2025 data.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey
insights.so_what: Agent fleets may carry a hidden human cost not yet captured in data.
insights.locator: How many of you are managing a fleet of agents right now?

insights.claim: DORA saw the same J-curve with cloud and SRE: things got a little better, then much worse, then organizations learned to use the technology, but how to reach the other side with AI is still being learned.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey
insights.so_what: History suggests AI productivity gains arrive after an adaptation trough.
insights.locator: There is another side. We've seen this all before.

insights.claim: Across eight factors including team performance, product performance, effectiveness, friction and burnout, DORA found seven distinct team profiles even though at least 90% of respondents use AI, implying AI itself does not explain performance differences.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey
insights.so_what: Variation in outcomes stems from how teams work, not from AI access.
insights.locator: What we also found were that there were seven unique team profiles

insights.claim: The 'constrained by process' profile shows high burnout and friction, low effectiveness and valuable-work time, relatively low instability and slightly lower throughput, while 'harmonious high achievers' deliver high-quality work sustainably in a low-friction, stable environment.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey
insights.so_what: Team archetypes help leaders diagnose where AI will amplify problems.
insights.locator: Let's look at two of the different groups here.

insights.claim: DORA identified seven capabilities that combined with AI adoption drive better outcomes; the talk walks through six: a clear and communicated AI stance, a healthy data ecosystem with internal data access, strong version control, working in small batches, user-centric focus, and quality internal platforms.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey
insights.so_what: Capabilities, not tool purchases, determine whether adoption becomes value.
insights.quote: seven capabilities that when combined together with adoption, drive better outcomes
insights.locator: What we identified were seven capabilities

insights.claim: Harvey tells organisations to stop measuring lines of code generated by AI, saying adoption metrics suffice only to answer a board's first question, and returns require capabilities beyond adoption.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey
insights.so_what: Replace vanity output metrics with outcome metrics such as stability and throughput.
insights.quote: stop measuring how many lines did the AI generate
insights.locator: For the love of whatever you view as good and holy

insights.claim: Without a clear stance on which AI can be used where, employees either avoid AI or use it covertly from home experience while fearing being fired, causing friction.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey
insights.so_what: Publish explicit AI usage policy to reduce shadow usage and risk.
insights.locator: We've got a clear and communicated stance.

insights.claim: Strong version control (commit and roll back) and working in small batches matter more with AI because agents can go down bad paths and bots produce 50,000-line pull requests, while smaller well-defined tasks help agents too.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey
insights.so_what: Smaller changes and fast rollback contain AI-induced instability.
insights.locator: If DORA has found nothing else

insights.claim: Teams with a user-centric focus see performance improve with AI, and those without see it decrease; faster prototyping lets teams build many options and run A-B-C-D-E-F-G tests rather than commit to one.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey
insights.so_what: AI shifts advantage toward product discovery speed and experimentation.
insights.locator: One of the things that we found in our research

insights.claim: Quality internal platforms turn AI adoption into value, and platform customers now include agents, so agent experience (documentation, agent files) joins developer experience, though one cited paper found agent files do not clearly improve output.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey
insights.so_what: Platform engineering scope is widening to agents and non-developer builders.
insights.locator: The other thing that probably isn't a surprise

insights.claim: Harvey suggests platform teams should shift engineering capacity from shipping the next feature toward enabling builders such as non-engineers, treating shadow IT as a signal of unmet business problems.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey
insights.so_what: Governance of citizen-built software becomes a platform engineering mandate.
insights.locator: Shadow IT, we should feel bad when there's shadow IT.

insights.claim: Harvey argues code reviews, which exist to check tests, teach and share knowledge, may now be a bottleneck that guardrails, automated tests, LLM-assisted learning and synchronous pairing can replace, and engineering capacity would be better spent on guardrails and intent.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey
insights.so_what: If review is the new bottleneck, expect tooling investment in automated validation to rise.
insights.quote: Maybe it's time code reviews go away.
insights.locator: How many of you feel like code reviews are the new bottleneck?

insights.claim: Harvey favours Kaizen (continuous improvement) over Kaikaku (radical change) generally, citing Deming that a bad system beats a good person every time, yet makes code review removal the radical exception.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey
insights.so_what: Incremental system improvement is the baseline approach to AI adoption.
insights.quote: A bad system will beat a good person every single time.
insights.locator: A bad system will beat a good person every single time.

insights.claim: Harvey urges organisations to treat DORA findings as hypotheses to test in their own context and join the DORA community, since findings come from the world, not a given business unit.
insights.speaker: Nathen Harvey
insights.so_what: Run local experiments rather than copying benchmark conclusions.
insights.quote: Take our findings and use them as your hypothesis.
insights.locator: I want to close out with some final thoughts.
